Earlier this summer, Archie and Lilibet joined their parents for a trip to Britain during which they reunited with Charles and Camilla at Highgrove House.

The children also visited Althorp, the childhood home and final resting place of Harry’s late mother, Princess Diana. They were joined by Harry’s uncle and Diana’s brother Charles Spencer, and members of the late Princess of Wales’ family.

Schofield told Fox News Digital that whether the move becomes a reset or another source of royal tension may depend on how quietly the Sussexes are able to navigate school life, security concerns and public interest.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Harry and Meghan’s challenge will be resisting the temptation to turn every uncomfortable moment into another confrontation," she said. "If they can quietly establish boundaries and allow their children to settle, that could actually help relations with the Royal Family."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"If Britain once again becomes the setting for constant disputes about security, photographers, and the press, it risks reopening exactly the tensions everyone supposedly wants to leave behind," Schofield continued.

Schofield added, "Harry and Meghan cannot realistically expect all of the significance associated with their royal identities while expecting the attention attached to those identities to disappear. The real test of this move will be whether they have finally accepted that distinction."

item.title: Ted Cruz names ‘most powerful Democrat’ as he warns socialist rise has paralyzed bipartisanship
item.description: Sen. Ted Cruz claims Chuck Schumer is "truly terrified" of the extreme left, warning that progressive momentum is paralyzing bipartisan work.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, believes that fear of a rising wave of progressives is paralyzing possible bipartisan work on permitting reform that would otherwise create fertile ground for collaboration.

"That dynamic is dangerous right now because they are terrified of the extreme left. Finding a middle ground on ideological issues right now is … the prospects for success, particularly between now and election day, are not high," Cruz said at an energy summit hosted by Club for Growth and Arnold Ventures on Thursday.

"Schumer is truly terrified right now," he added, referring to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y.

Cruz’s political assessment underscores what progressive momentum in the 2026 midterms means for more establishment figures in the Democratic Party — and especially the ones already in Congress — and the policy areas that legislators may still want to address before the November midterm elections.

CRUZ SAYS MAMDANI, AOC, PLATNER SHOW DEMOCRATS' LEFTWARD SHIFT: 'THAT'S WHERE THE ENERGY IS'

"They’re in the middle of a revolution," Cruz said. "Their problem is that they’re very driven by their interest groups. They’re captured by their activists."

His remarks came as he delivered an address at an energy affordability summit hosted by the Club for Growth, a free-market group that advocates for limited government. In particular, the event centered on permitting reform, an area where Democrats and Republicans have found some overlap.

Although differences remain about just how far to scale back regulations or how far to push legislative changes, lawmakers at the event stressed that bipartisan work on cutting back red tape could meaningfully expand American access to energy projects domestically.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted how regulatory bodies had prevented the expansion of nuclear energy — a source of power that is uniting Republicans and Democrats as a new frontier in a space apart from fossil fuels.

"We have built three new nuclear reactors in like the last 40 years. It went quickly from: we didn’t even know about the technology, to 20% of U.S. electric generation from nuclear reactors," Wright said.

100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY

"We created the Nuclear Regulatory Commission… in the name of safety, no malintent. But since that creation, we’ve built almost no reactors in the United States since. If it’s so uncertain and so long to permit something, it’s just not worth investing in. That’s awful! Nuclear is just an awesome energy technology."

Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio., stressed that many of the discussions around reform have come down to a matter of practical details.

"There's a lot of conversations going on not about who's going to fight with whom or who is going to take credit for it, but rather what is the mechanics of getting it done," Moreno said at the Club for Growth event.

"When it comes to permitting reform, if we can actually pull this off, Scott, what does it mean? It means lower energy prices for all Americans, us taking better care of our environment, being good stewards for the next generation. Those are worthy goals that should unite all of us, and I'm hopeful that we can get that done," Moreno said, speaking to conservative political commentator Scott Jennings, a moderator at the event.

Despite a sense of optimism among several speakers — and even from Cruz himself — Cruz warned listeners that progressives already have a very real presence inside the Capitol that casts a shadow on permitting reform and other areas.

"It is not the case that every Senate Democrat is a Marxist or Islamist. What is the case is that every Senate Democrat is terrified of the Marxists and Islamists. Because that’s where the energy is in their party, that’s where the power is, that’s where the money is; it's where the young people are. I think Mamdani is the single most powerful Democrat in the country," Cruz said, referring to the socialist mayor of New York City, Zohran Mamdani.

Since Mamdani, a self-proclaimed socialist, came to power earlier this year, a series of progressive candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) have won key primary races and even toppled veteran incumbents.

A few notable races include New York's socialist Darializa Avila Chevalier and her victory over incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., the veteran chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus. Along those lines, Melat Kiros, another socialist in Colorado, unseated 30-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette, D-Colo.

SCHUMER DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER DSA BELONGS IN DEMOCRATIC PARTY

With pressures like that, Cruz argued that it’s difficult to find legislators who are willing to separate themselves from progressives.

He believes there isn’t leadership to push back against that progressive momentum.

"Look, Schumer is known for a lot of things but acts of principle and courage are not among them," Cruz said.

item.title: ESPN risks all of its anti-woke progress by rehiring controversial host Stan Verrett
item.description: ESPN rehired Stan Verrett for NFL Network despite his history of divisive social media posts, raising questions about Burke Magnus' editorial standards.
item.content:encoded:
The perception in and around ESPN is that management has tried to distance itself from the divisive, political rhetoric that defined the network over the past decade. Executive vice president Burke Magnus has led the effort.

Magnus has elevated personalities who provide a more positive, fan-focused perspective on sports, from Pat McAfee and Peter Schrager to Josh Pate and Jason McCourty.

The network parted ways with several commentators and declined to renew the contracts of others who frequently generated headlines for comments critics considered toxic or political, including Ryan Clark, Mark Jones, Clinton Yates, Sarah Spain and Max Kellerman.

Magnus's actions sent a message to current and future employees. Self-serving commentary and social media activity that undermine the company's reputation are no longer tolerated.

Viewers have noticed. Nearly every one of ESPN’s daily studio shows has gained viewership year over year. For that, Magnus deserves credit.

DAN LE BATARD THINKS THERE ARE TOO MANY WHITE NFL ANALYSTS, DESPITE THE RACIAL MAKEUP OF HIS OWN COMPANY

And yet, his latest decision undermines his own edict, suggesting to employees that the very behavior he has spent the past two years eliminating is again welcome.

On Thursday, ESPN announced that it had rehired Stan Verrett to host a daily show on its sister network, NFL Network. Sources tell OutKick that Magnus and executive Mike McQuade chose Verrett for the role.

The move is notable because ESPN did not renew Verrett’s contract last year. Verrett claimed the departure was his decision. Sources have told OutKick otherwise. Either way, ESPN is bringing him back despite knowing how he conducted himself during his previous tenure.

Perhaps no recent ESPN employee behaved less professionally on social media than Verrett. We would know. 

For years, Verrett tweeted obsessively about us, predicted our demise, denounced us as racist, and directly messaged me "f--- you" after following me.

Some of those posts are below:

Below is a friendly back-and-forth between SportsCenter anchor Nicole Briscoe and me about President Trump. Verrett inserted himself into the mentions by spreading unprompted racial hysteria.

"I can help here, Nicole. [Burack] works for a site [OutKick] that uses some of the same kind of racially-tinged rhetoric to attract a specific audience to try to get them to gamble. Plausible deniability is the escape hatch for all the foolishness."

Huh?

It wasn't just us.

Verrett spent much of his final years at ESPN picking social media fights with people who voiced even mildly conservative opinions. In many cases, he dismissed arguments he disliked as — wait for it — racist.

Verrett told former college football player T.J. Moe that white people like him have "every advantage available in this society" because Moe rejected the idea that white moviegoers care about the skin color of performers.

"No, Black people support other Black people because if we didn’t, history tells us they might not get any support at all. We know you’re not going to do it, based on your whining. Quit tying so hard to be a victim. You have every advantage available in this society."

Verrett’s sports commentary isn’t much different.

ESPN is privately dissatisfied with its WNBA coverage, particularly the negative tone and racial emphasis some of its commentators have attached to the league. Verrett is unlikely to help address those concerns.

He recently got into a spat with an anonymous account with roughly 150 followers, arguing that biases help explain Caitlin Clark’s popularity among white people and Middle America.

"If you worry about people thinking you’re racist for supporting Clark, that’s between you and your mirror. Rational, honest people understand that a part of her appeal is to middle America, particularly white people in middle America. And that’s fine. But people lie and pretend it has nothing to do with it ..."

Perhaps Magnus forgot when he re-hired Verrett that white people and Middle Americans watch sports, too.

Verrett also regularly seeks responses from Dave Portnoy, Clay Travis, Jason Whitlock and Megyn Kelly, reminding viewers of his contempt for prominent figures who represent the views of roughly half the country.

Notably, he took issue with one of Travis’ posts advocating against transgender athletes competing in female sports:

So, the question is why. Why would Magnus and McQuade hire Verrett back?

ESPN has younger anchors on its roster. It could have used NFL Network, which draws fewer than 100,000 viewers in most time slots, as a proving ground for up-and-coming talent. Instead, it turned to Verrett, a 60-year-old anchor who is significantly older than the channel’s average viewer."

It’s difficult to see the upside in hiring someone with such a documented history of alienating a substantial portion of the country. His public persona runs directly counter to ESPN’s stated preference for avoiding unnecessary conflict.

OutKick asked ESPN on Thursday why it hired Verrett. The network did not provide a clear response. However, the timing raises questions about whether recent criticism of Magnus influenced the decision.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Last month, OutKick first reported that ESPN was laying off Ryan Clark. After Clark’s dismissal, the influential radio show "The Breakfast Club" claimed that Magnus leaked the information to OutKick to embarrass Clark by having him fired in the middle of his show.

To be clear, Magnus was not our source. It's unclear why ESPN informed Clark of his exit during a commercial break of "NFL Live," after learning OutKick planned to report it later in the day.

Later that week, Clark repeatedly described Magnus on his podcast as the executive who did not like him and suggested Magnus may have had a problem with "how black" Clark says he was.

"I couldn’t be too black [at ESPN]," Clark said.

Clark offered no evidence that Magnus’ decision was motivated by race. More plausible explanations for why ESPN dismissed him include Clark’s on-air belittling of colleague Peter Schrager, his criticism of Robert Griffin III’s marriage to a white woman, and his retraction of unsupported claims about Louisiana law enforcement officers.

Nonetheless, Clark’s comments created a narrative among certain audiences, including The Breakfast Club, Threads and Bluesky.

Such accusations, while unsupported, undoubtedly place Magnus, a top Disney executive, in an uncomfortable position.

For years, we’ve watched executives respond to similarly unfounded allegations of racism by making decisions intended to demonstrate that the allegations are untrue.

Rehiring Stan Verrett, who had employed much of the same racial rhetoric as Clark, could help Magnus refute that narrative.

Interestingly, Jemele Hill said on YouTube that Clark spent time with her and Verrett after leaving ESPN.

We asked ESPN whether the criticism of Magnus played any role in the decision to bring back Verrett. We did not receive a response.

In any event, Magnus weakened the standard he set by hiring Verrett.

Notice that ESPN had not generated its usual wave of negative headlines for veering away from sports in recent months. Magnus had almost entirely eradicated the type of commentary that divided fans along political and racial lines.

Ryan Clark's firing confirmed Magnus's vision. Employees received the message.

Yet, by rehiring Stan Verrett, employees will naturally wonder whether fighting on X and reflexively accusing critics of racism is back in style. How could they not?

The addition is disappointing for sports fans.

NFL Network was created for football fans of all demographics. Now, the channel is showcasing someone with a documented history of expressing hostility toward a significant portion of that audience.

Burke Magnus deserves credit for the improved state of ESPN. That's on him. He also deserves scrutiny for this decision, one that could undermine the culture he worked so hard to improve.

item.title: Rutgers suffers worst defeat of Greg Schiano's second stint, losing to UMass who hadn't won since 2024
item.description: UMass scored 30 straight points to stun Greg Schiano's Rutgers 37-21 in Piscataway, New Jersey, the worst loss of his second stint as head coach.
item.content:encoded:
College football returns in full force this week and someone should have told the boys up in Piscataway, New Jersey.

The Rutgers Scarlet Knights entered their first game of the 2026 season as 29.5-point favorites (by some books) over the UMass Minutemen, who failed to win a single game last season and haven’t put a W on the board since Oct. 26, 2024.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

As it turned out Thursday night, Greg Schiano and the rest of New Jersey found out just how strong the Minutemen were. UMass scored 30 straight points on the Rutgers’ defense before the Scarlet Knights could get back to the end zone. By the time quarterback Dylan Lonergan found wide receiver KJ Duff to make the game 30-14, there was just over 7 minutes left in the contest.

UMass got the touchdown back and finished off Rutgers for the win, 37-21.

It wasn’t just the run-of-the-mill loss for Rutgers.

Since Schiano reclaimed the reins as head coach before the 2020 season, the Scarlet Knights have had success against opponents outside of the Big Ten Conference. They beat Ohio, Miami (Ohio) and Norfolk State in 2025, Howard, Akron and Virginia Tech to start 2024 and Temple, Virginia Tech and Howard in 2023.

In fact, Rutgers hadn’t lost to a non-conference opponent outside of a bowl game since 2019 when they fell to Boston College.

Schiano has had the ability to revive the energy around Rutgers football since 2020. He had Jim Harbaugh’s Michigan team on the ropes in November 2020, the team beat Miami (FL) in the 2023 Pinstripe Bowl and knocked off Washington at home in 2024.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

But as fireworks sounded over Middlesex County on Thursday night, it felt like any kind of momentum that may have been garnered over the course of a few good seasons came to a full stop.

Regardless of how UMass may have rebuilt its football team over the last few months, there’s simply no excuse for New Jersey’s top FBS school to fall to a team that had gone winless all of 2025.

It is, in fact, the worst loss of Schiano’s second stint as Rutgers head coach. Long gone are the days of A-list celebrities like James Gandolfini gracing Shi Stadium with their presence. The time is now for Rutgers to right the ship. Next week, they hit the road against Boston College.

One win can eliminate a lot of bad energy. It has to start there before calling 2026 completely lost.

item.title: Viral bakery's missing cinnamon rolls spark $3,100 theft accusation and Border Patrol plot twist
item.description: A viral cinnamon rolls theft accusation took a shocking turn when police revealed the Uber driver was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol during a delivery run.
item.content:encoded:
What began as a case of hundreds of missing cinnamon rolls and an alleged $3,100 theft took an unexpected turn when police determined the delivery driver hadn't stolen them at all: He had been arrested by U.S. Border Patrol on his way to make the delivery.

Julie Pierre, the 21-year-old owner of Sunrise, Florida-based Roll & Dough, hired an Uber courier on Aug. 22 to deliver about 350 of her viral cinnamon rolls to the Yellow Green Farmers Market in nearby Hollywood, according to the South Florida Sun Sentinel.

The order never arrived.

NAKED DOORDASH DRIVER DELIVERS FOOD TO TEXAS HOME IN SHOCKING SECURITY CAMERA VIDEO

Unable to reach the driver, Pierre initially believed he had taken off with thousands of dollars in merchandise. She shared the apparent theft with her hundreds of thousands of social media followers — drawing widespread attention to the missing pastries.

But Sunrise police said there was no theft.

"The investigation determined that a theft did not occur," Sunrise Police Officer Victor Fortune told Fox News Digital.

Instead, the delivery driver was stopped and taken into custody by U.S. Border Patrol in Hollywood while he was still on his way to the delivery destination, Fortune said.

Border Patrol identified the driver as Ivan Dario Rico Molano, a Colombian citizen.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Agents stopped a silver Kia Carnival just before 9 a.m. Aug. 22 on southbound Interstate 95 after a records check showed the vehicle's registered owner was an immigrant without legal status, a U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

During the encounter, Molano acknowledged being in the U.S. without legal authorization, according to the CBP. 

The agency said he entered the country legally in May 2021 but remained beyond his authorized period of stay.

Molano was arrested and taken to a Border Patrol station for processing, according to the CBP.

The cinnamon rolls, meanwhile, stayed behind.

During the encounter, Molano was allowed to contact another person to take possession of the vehicle, which still contained the cinnamon rolls and their storage containers, Fortune said.

That person later contacted Sunrise police to arrange to return the items, Fortune said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

On Aug. 27 — five days after the rolls were supposed to reach the farmers market — Sunrise police recovered the cinnamon rolls and containers and returned them to Pierre.

By then, however, the pastries could no longer be sold and had to be discarded, Pierre told the Sun Sentinel.

"We're still out $3,100," Pierre said. "Stolen or not, we suffered a loss."

Attempts by Fox News Digital to contact Pierre for comment were unsuccessful.

The bizarre explanation brought an end to an episode that generated widespread attention online after Pierre initially accused the courier of stealing the order.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Pierre subsequently corrected the allegation after learning from police what had happened.

In a statement posted on Instagram, the bakery apologized for describing the incident as a theft "before learning the complete circumstances."

The statement also stressed that Pierre's report to police did not lead to Molano's arrest.

item.title: US adversary turns up the heat on America’s AI lead with an underestimated edge
item.description: China's "East Data, West Computing" initiative is rapidly expanding AI infrastructure, but a major chip constraint complicates Beijing's push.
item.content:encoded:
China is racing to build the data centers and energy infrastructure needed to power artificial intelligence, raising concerns that Beijing’s ability to rapidly construct massive projects could help it get closer to America’s commanding lead in the physical infrastructure underpinning the AI race.

The U.S. remains far ahead in sheer numbers. The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence’s 2026 AI Index, using Cloudscene data, counted 5,427 U.S. data centers in 2025 compared with 449 in China. Stanford cautioned that the count does not account for differences in facility size, computing capacity or utilization.

But China is moving quickly.

AMERICA IS FIGHTING YESTERDAY’S AI WAR. TOMORROW’S WAR IS ON THE WAY

"We know that China is far behind, but we also know that they are moving at great speed," China expert Gordon Chang told Fox News Digital.

Chang argued that Beijing understands the U.S. advantage will be difficult to erase if America continues building at the same pace and said growing opposition to data-center development could slow that expansion.

President Donald Trump made a similar argument this week, warning communities fighting new projects that China stands to benefit.

"China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!" Trump also argued that communities embracing data centers would gain jobs and tax revenues.

Vice President JD Vance sharpened that warning Thursday, telling FOX Business there was "a very good chance" the U.S. could lose the AI race to China if Democrats regain control of Congress.

Vance said the broader problem is America’s ability to build enough power to support data centers and other major infrastructure. "We cannot be a country that says we’re not going to build more power," Vance said, arguing that the administration is trying to make it easier to construct power plants alongside data centers while protecting residential ratepayers from higher electricity costs.

AI BOOM: DEMAND FOR DATA CENTERS DRIVES INNOVATION BY ENERGY, TECH INDUSTRIES TO PRODUCE NEW POWER SOURCES

He also pointed to the widening U.S.-China electricity gap, saying China now generates roughly three times as much power as the United States. "We’ve got to build more power plants. We’ve got to make the regulatory state easier to work with."

Asked about China’s rapid infrastructure expansion, the Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the premise that AI should primarily be viewed as a geopolitical contest.

"AI should not be owned by major countries, still less dominated by contests and rivalry," Embassy spokesperson Liu Chang told Fox News Digital.

Liu pointed to China’s 2025 Global AI Governance Action Plan, which calls for accelerating construction of clean power, next-generation networks, computing capacity and data centers. He said China advocates cooperation with the U.S. and wants AI development to benefit both countries and the broader international community.

Behind that diplomatic message, Beijing is undertaking a massive geographic reorganization of its computing infrastructure.

Under China’s "East Data, West Computing" initiative, Beijing is directing more computing capacity toward western regions where land is available and wind and solar resources can help reduce energy costs.

Five of China’s eight national computing hubs are located in western China, according to a June 25 report from the government-backed Digital China initiative. More than 30 data centers were under construction within a three-kilometer area in Horinger, Inner Mongolia, while intensive construction was also underway in Zhongwei, Ningxia.

That buildout caught the attention of members of the bipartisan US-China Economic and Security Review Commission during a recent fact-finding trip to China.

"I left with an intense belief that the Chinese see this as the frontier in terms of competition," Commission Vice Chairman Mike Kuiken told Fox News Digital, describing AI as increasingly intertwined with robotics, biotechnology, advanced materials and manufacturing.

Kuiken said China has one significant advantage when it comes to constructing the infrastructure needed to support that technology.

"The Chinese, because they write the rules as they go, and the rule of law largely does not exist, are able to just move faster in terms of building things," he said.

But Kuiken also identified a major Chinese weakness: access to the most advanced chips.

"The constraints that are real though, the Chinese do not have the ability to procure advanced chips," he said, while describing Beijing’s ability to rapidly construct coal plants and other infrastructure as "quite incredible."

THE WAR ON DATA CENTERS JEOPARDIZES OUR ECONOMY AND NATIONAL SECURITY

The U.S. retains major advantages beyond its data-center lead. The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence’s 2026 AI Index found that America produced 59 notable AI models in 2025 compared with 35 from China, and U.S. private AI investment reached $285.9 billion, compared with $12.4 billion in China. Stanford cautioned that private investment figures understate Beijing’s overall spending because of Chinese government-backed funds.

At the same time, Chinese models have rapidly narrowed the performance gap. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index found that as of March 2026, the top U.S. model led the top Chinese model by just 2.7%.

Chang also alleged that Beijing is seeking to exploit American opposition to data centers and claimed China-linked networks have helped support protests against projects in the US. "These protests are not entirely organic," Chang told Fox News Digital.

Kuiken was cautious about portraying those local disputes as part of a broader anti-China fight, saying genuine U.S. opposition to data-center projects has also emerged over concerns including electricity costs, water use, noise and land development.

"We are building things in the U.S. faster than we have in a long time," he said, adding that policymakers are working through infrastructure constraints. "Usually there are local issues that are driving those things."

The emerging competition, therefore, is not simply over who develops the smartest AI model.

It is increasingly a race over who can build the electricity, data centers, chips and networks needed to run those models at enormous scale — and how quickly they can build them.

item.title: Trump trade chief reveals what preceded Canada walking away from 'best deal in the world'
item.description: Jamieson Greer says Canada walked away from a handshake deal with President Trump on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber, then demanded even more.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's top trade advisor, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, said Canada walked away from the "best deal in the world" after the nation declined to finalize a trade agreement with the U.S. nearly two weeks ago.

Greer joined "Special Report" on Thursday to detail the negotiations that preceded the contentious trade fight between the U.S. and its northern neighbor.

"We offered them the best deal. They looked at it square in the face and turned around," he said on "Special Report."

Greer’s comments come amid a fierce trade war between the U.S. and Canada that Trump further escalated by signing an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America."

TRUMP'S CANADA TARIFF FIGHT REACHES CRITICAL POINT AS HOUSE GOP SUMMONS TRADE CHIEF

The trade chief said that although Trump’s trade program already gives Canada "the best deal," U.S. officials were willing to negotiate after Canadian authorities approached the administration seeking a revised agreement.

"I told them what we could deliver. I said, ‘We could try to give you the best deal in the world on steel, aluminum, autos and help you out on lumber,’" Greer told Fox News. "These are things very sensitive for the Canadians, and we managed to move the levers of our government to give them that deal."

FEARS OF A CANADIAN TRADE WAR ARE OVERBLOWN. SO FAR, IT’S MORE OF A SKIRMISH

After Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney reached the handshake agreement, Canadian officials returned to Ottawa. Greer said he remains unsure what transpired there that ultimately prompted Canada to renege on the deal and seek additional concessions.

"When they came back, they wanted more, they wanted more tariff relief. It wasn't good enough to have the best deal in the world," he told Fox News chief political anchor Bret Baier. "They wanted it to be even better… These are things we couldn't accommodate."

DAVID MARCUS: CANADA SEES TRUMP TRADE WAR AS ‘LIFE AND DEATH’ WHILE AMERICANS BARELY NOTICE

Canada suspended trade talks on Aug. 21. U.S. trade officials blamed the breakdown on what they described as "new demands and walk backs of other commitments by Canada" that "upended the careful balance" of the negotiations.

"We were ready to do it. We gave them the best deal in the world. Did it give them everything? No. Did we have everything we wanted? No. That's how a deal works," Greer said.

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

The trade chief said Canadian leaders appeared on television after the agreement fell apart and claimed the country had "been attacked."

Greer pushed back on that characterization, arguing that the "vast majority" of Canadian goods enter the U.S. duty-free and noting that Canada, along with China, are the only countries to have retaliated against U.S. trade measures.

"Since even before the second Trump term, they've limited our ability to sell dairy into Canada, and they're importing things from China," he said. "They're turning them into other goods and trying to get them duty-free across our border."

Greer, who believes the Canadians were negotiating in good faith, said he has received some outreach from Canada but no formal negotiations since Aug. 21.

As for what comes next, Greer said the trade deal’s future now lies "in Canada’s corner."

item.title: Maryland sheriff torches Democrats over law he says puts illegal immigrants first
item.description: Sheriff Jeffrey Gahler warns Maryland's Community Trust Act could force jails to release dangerous illegal immigrants flagged by ICE back onto streets.
item.content:encoded:
A Maryland sheriff is warning that the state’s new sanctuary law could put dangerous illegal immigrants back on the streets and leave more American families mourning crimes he says could have been prevented.

"It’s just a matter of time," Harford County Sheriff Jeffrey Gahler told Fox News Digital, warning that the restrictions will lead to more crime and more victims.

Gahler delivered the blunt warning after testifying before a House Judiciary subcommittee about Maryland’s restrictions on cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities. He is also leading 16 fellow sheriffs, representing two-thirds of the state, in a lawsuit challenging the Community Trust Act.

The 40-year law enforcement veteran said his greatest fear is that the law will force correctional officers to release an illegal immigrant from jail even after U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement has flagged that person as a public safety or national security threat.

MARYLAND SHERIFFS SHOULD NOT BE HANDCUFFED BY RECKLESS SANCTUARY POLITICS

Gahler said the law could force jail officials to release an inmate who is otherwise eligible to leave local custody instead of transferring that person directly to ICE.

HUNDREDS OF JAILED ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED BACK ONTO BLUE-STATE STREETS DESPITE ICE DETAINERS, RECORDS SHOW

"I don’t want to have to open the jail door and say, ‘Welcome back to Harford County. Go victimize. Let’s create some more victims,’" he said. "That is insane."

If someone released under the law commits another crime, Gahler said responsibility would rest with the elected officials who imposed the restrictions.

ANGEL MOM WARNS DEMOCRATS 'WE'RE NOT GOING TO STOP' AFTER EMOTIONAL HOUSE HEARING ON SANCTUARY POLICIES

"So whose hands is it on?" he said. "The politicians."

Gahler said he testified to give lawmakers a view from the front lines after years of warnings from law enforcement leaders. He accused state officials of understanding the risks but choosing politics over public safety.

SPANBERGER'S ICE RESTRICTIONS DEALT MAJOR SETBACK AS JUDGE WARNS OTHER BLUE STATES

"I think they understand. I think they don’t care," Gahler said. "Those who are on the side of the issue supporting criminal illegal immigration, who voted for this nonsense of ending our agreements and coming up with the Community Trust Act … they do not care."

"We have a criminal-friendly legislature," he added. "It’s all pro-criminal."

Gahler pointed to two families in his county whose lives were shattered by illegal immigrant killers.

EXCLUSIVE: ANGEL DAD FINDS ‘NEW PURPOSE’ WITH ICE AFTER DAUGHTER’S KILLING TURNED HIS WORLD UPSIDE DOWN

Rachel Morin, a 37-year-old mother of five, was raped and murdered on the Ma and Pa Trail in Bel Air in August 2023. Victor Antonio Martinez-Hernandez, an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, was convicted and sentenced to life without parole.

Kayla Hamilton, a 20-year-old autistic woman, was raped and strangled inside her Aberdeen home in July 2022. Walter Javier Martinez, a suspected MS-13 member from El Salvador who entered the U.S. illegally as an unaccompanied minor, was sentenced to life in prison, with all but 70 years suspended.

Gahler said neither woman should be reduced to a political talking point and accused supporters of Maryland’s immigration restrictions of failing to show genuine concern for their families.

"No one called Patty Morin" after Rachel’s murder, Gahler said. He added that no one contacted Kayla’s mother, Tammy Nobles, to express condolences or promise to fight for the two Harford County victims.

HOCHUL ICE POLICY ‘WRITTEN IN THE BLOOD OF VICTIMS,’ OPPONENT SAYS AS SHERIFFS SUE

"I simply think that there are those in Annapolis and those in Washington who do not care," he added. "It’s politics over public safety."

The Community Trust Act limits when Maryland authorities can question people about their immigration status, hold them over suspected civil violations or notify ICE that they are in custody.

Gov. Wes Moore allowed the measure to become law without his signature.

"Maryland will never be a sanctuary for criminals under Governor Moore," Rhyan Lake, Senior Communications Strategist for Moore, said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "In fact, since Governor Moore took office, Maryland is seeing some of the largest drops in violent crime in the country."

"We will always work with the federal administration when it comes to making our communities safer, but untrained, unqualified, and unaccountable ICE agents arresting five-year-olds and ripping mothers from their families does not make anyone safer," Lake continued. "In Maryland, we’ll continue holding violent offenders accountable and protecting Marylanders’ constitutional rights and basic dignity."

Gahler and the other sheriffs argue that the restrictions dismantled a safe, jail-based partnership with ICE under the federal 287(g) program. He stressed that his deputies were not conducting immigration raids or doing the work of federal agents.

"We do not do ICE’s job for them," Gahler said. "We work with our federal partners. We don’t replace our federal partners."

He said the program applied to people already jailed on criminal allegations and allowed ICE transfers to occur inside the secure facility instead of through potentially more dangerous arrests after their release.

"Our 287(g) program identified those people who were here committing criminal offenses against our citizens and are in the country illegally," Gahler said. "Then we turned them over safely in the security and safety of our jail after they were already in custody."

"Anytime we don’t have to do a raid in law enforcement, it’s safer," he added. "You have the person secured. Turn them over to ICE because ICE says they pose a threat to public safety or national security."

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

Gahler said opposition to the program has ebbed and flowed with the political climate. He noted that Harford County joined under President Barack Obama, but said Maryland critics renewed their opposition when President Donald Trump returned to the White House.

"They’re doing it for purely political reasons and not public safety," Gahler said. "That’s complete nonsense."

He compared Maryland with California, saying the two Democrat-led states appeared to be competing over policies he believes favor offenders over victims.

"I look at Maryland and California as playing a game of tennis," Gahler said, accusing the states of "whacking the ball back and forth across the court to see who can be more idiotic."

NEW YORK SHERIFFS 'MAD AS HELL' AS HOCHUL PUSHES TO BAN KEY LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERSHIP

The sheriff also tied his fight to the approaching 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. A Maryland State Police commander on 9/11, Gahler said the tragedy exposed deadly communication gaps among law enforcement agencies, barriers he believes Maryland is now rebuilding.

"The complete takeaway from 9/11 was that we didn’t communicate" effectively across local, state and federal agencies, Gahler said. Yet 25 years later, he argued, Maryland has moved dangerously far from that lesson.

"The Community Trust Act … forbids us from talking to a federal law enforcement partner," he continued. "It doesn’t get any more stupid than that. When you see terrible legislation, that’s as bad as it gets."

Gahler said the sheriffs will keep pressing their case in court and speaking out for victims. Unless state leaders change course, he warned, more families will join a grim and growing list.

"Our job should be to stop increasing the number of angel families," Gahler said, "and stop allowing American citizens to be the victims of crime committed by people who are in our country illegally."
 
Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

item.title: Tennessee official says Flock CEO should be hanged 'publicly for treason’ as controversial cameras face revolt
item.description: Joe Carr called for Flock Safety's CEO to be hanged for treason at a public meeting, igniting a national debate over automated license plate readers.
item.content:encoded:
A Tennessee county commissioner is going viral after he told a Flock Safety representative at a public meeting that the company's CEO should be hanged for treason, marking a fever-pitch surrounding personal privacy and open public hostility over the nationwide rollout of the controversial surveillance tools.

"I believe that Flock right now is one of the most hated companies in America. They are one of the most corrupt companies in America," Kingsport Commissioner Joe Carr told a Flock Safety representative at an Aug. 13 work session.

"Quite frankly, sir, I don't think we can make America great again without hanging your CEO publicly for treason," Carr continued. "Your company is an enemy of the American people."

‘DARTH VADER’ USES DARK SIDE TO MOCK CONTROVERSIAL SURVEILLANCE CAMERAS: 'THE EMPEROR IS A FAN OF FLOCK'

His comments were quickly interrupted by the leader of the commission meeting, who interjected, saying, "Mr. Carr, we are not going to threaten violence to anybody."

Speaking with Fox News Digital, Carr looked to clarify his now-viral remarks.

FLOCK SAFETY CAMERAS NEED CONSTITUTIONAL GUARDRAILS BEFORE FURTHER DEPLOYMENT, TENNESSEE MAYOR ARGUES

"I didn't call for lynchings, I called for due process," Carr said. "You want to try the guy first, and I don't support political random killings. I definitely don't. But at the same time, you know, the American people are angry. I felt, and I think a lot of them felt, that no elected official was really going hard enough on this. And so I wanted to be the guy to do that."

Carr's criticism comes as Flock's rollout of automated license plate readers draws national scrutiny over government surveillance, data security and personal privacy. Roughly 100 municipalities have canceled or deactivated their contracts with the security company.

POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN'

"I think probably the biggest story though isn't really my comments, but people's reaction to them," Carr said. "You can go on any of the posts about it and like 99 percent of the replies are agreeing with me. And I think that's where the American people are at right now."

"People have a right to go about their business without being spied on," he added. "Whether or not they're going to work or going to church, picking their kids up from school, going to football practice or whatever, they have a right to do all these things without being spied on and without having the government logging their every move."

TEXAS GOV GREG ABBOTT MOVES TO CUT STATE FUNDING FOR AI-POWERED FLOCK CAMERAS AMID PRIVACY CONCERNS

Within days of Carr’s comments in the work session, Sullivan County Sheriff Jeff Cassidy suspended the use of all 10 of Flock’s ALPRs in the county due to "legitimate concerns" surrounding "privacy, oversight, and government surveillance," according to a press release.

Cassidy went on to ask the Sullivan County Commission to consider placing a referendum on the next local ballot "that would allow voters to decide" if the sheriff’s office can reinstate the technology.

"I believe the safeguards currently in place within our agency provide clear guidelines for the proper use of this technology. If an employee abuses or misuses the technology, we will take quick and decisive action, up to and including termination or prosecution when warranted," the statement continued.

Despite the sheriff’s office’s assertion that the cameras had facilitated positive, crime-fighting results within the community — including an instance in which a Flock camera assisted in locating a child predator who had escaped federal custody in a neighboring city — Carr insists their risks outweigh the benefits.

THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?

"If you use this inappropriately or if it gets hacked, and it's a national security risk by a foreign actor, it could very quickly snowball and become something that outweighs all of the positives that have incurred up to that point," Carr told Fox News Digital.

"Or, Heaven forbid, you get a government that starts acting totalitarian," he continued. "And then they have the infrastructure in place, and you can't really get rid of it once it's there."

More than 135,000 ALPRs have been identified throughout the country, with roughly four of every five cameras belonging to Flock, according to data from DeFlock.org.

Flock’s website says the company has operational cameras — which sit perched atop roadside poles — in 49 states, with each one capturing a vehicle’s characteristics and license plate number as it passes.

TEENS ACCUSED OF DESTROYING FLOCK CAMERA UNTIL BATTERY EXPLODED, IGNITING FIRE NEAR HOMES: REPORT

The company insists the cameras do not record continuously or utilize facial recognition technology to identify individuals in a specific car. Its website adds that customers own the data in which Flock gathers and "every search requires a documented reason and is logged for review."

However, instances of police officers using the technology to track previous romantic partners have made headlines in recent months, with some concerned citizens taking matters into their own hands by covering the cameras or shooting them with guns.

Last month, NPR reported that Flock cameras have been vandalized in at least 36 states throughout the country, further fueling the debate surrounding if the technology is truly welcome in the communities in which they were placed.

LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS AT HOME DEPOT AND LOWE’S SPARK PRIVACY FEARS

Flock did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The company’s use of artificial intelligence continues to be a sticking point for critics of the cameras, with both Republicans and Democrats speaking out against the rollout of Flock’s technology.

"I mean, this has probably been one of the most unifying things that I’ve seen in my lifetime," Carr said, adding, "It’s not really a left or right issue, because I think the one thing that people really understand innately, even if they’re not expressing it, is that they wouldn’t trust their worst enemy with the technology."

The skepticism has been echoed by political leaders on both sides of the aisle.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott last week paused state funding for Flock cameras. In Florida, Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis warned against expanding a "digital AI surveillance state," and the state's Department of Transportation announced Monday that it was revoking existing permits for automated license plate readers within state highway rights-of-way.

Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro also hit back against the company, announcing he would encourage a bipartisan bill for an overall ban on Flock cameras throughout the state.

"We need to work together," Carr told Fox News Digital. "It doesn’t matter who’s pulling with us on this. We need to work together and make sure that our descendants aren’t spied on forever."

item.title: Blue state school district accused of defying Supreme Court, hiding gender transitions from parents
item.description: A New Jersey school district faces a lawsuit over its transgender policy allowing students to socially transition without ever notifying their parents.
item.content:encoded:
A New Jersey school district is being sued over a policy allowing students to change their name and gender identity at school without notifying their parents.

Under the School District of the Chathams' policy, students are able to change their name in official school records, use the bathrooms and locker rooms that align with their gender identity, and the school guidance counselor decides "whether, and to what extent" parents are involved in the decision.

The school's policy flies in the face of the Supreme Court's ruling in Mirabelli v. Bonta in March, which granted an injunction against California over state policies that keep students' gender identities confidential from parents while the issue works its way through the lower courts, according to Christopher Ferrara, senior counsel for the Thomas More Society, who filed the lawsuit.

"Well, the court has made clear in the Mirabelli case, and the Third Circuit has a decision along the same lines, that parents have standing to challenge a policy like this, which would hide a gender transition from the parents, whether or not the child is actually transitioning," Ferrara told Fox News Digital. "And the Supreme Court indicated that the reason parents have standing is that the parents are the objects of this policy."

"The policy provides that this information will be hidden from them, so they have the right to object to it, whether or not their particular child or children is at that moment being transitioned. And there's always a risk, of course, that the child under peer pressure, or the influence of teachers, or social media, will go along with this ridiculous trend and decide that his gender is not the biological one that parents believe is God-given and immutable, but some other gender."

Ferrara noted that the policy could have major consequences for students who aren't seeking to transition their gender because they could be forced to share locker rooms and bathrooms with members of the opposite sex.

Moms for Liberty CEO and founder Tina Descovich, whose organization is one of the plaintiffs in the lawsuit, also alleged that students who refuse to use other students' preferred pronouns could face disciplinary action under the school's code of conduct.

"They have a policy in the school district that will actually punish children that don't use the demanded new gender identity pronoun and name of another student," Descovich told Fox News Digital. "They can do that just one time on accident, and they can be punished up to suspension just for using the wrong pronoun or the wrong name of someone that is identifying as something other than they actually are."

Fox News Digital reached out to the School District of the Chathams for comment.

Along with Moms for America, two anonymous parents of elementary school-aged daughters are plaintiffs in the lawsuit, which was filed Aug. 24. The plaintiffs accuse the school of violating the parents' and students' First Amendment rights to free speech and religious liberty, as well as the Due Process Clause of the 14th Amendment. The school district is also accused of violating parental rights that were affirmed in the Supreme Court's ruling in Mahmoud v. Taylor, which determined that parents can opt their children out of LGBT-centered lessons.

WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE

"The Supreme Court has ruled twice on these issues," Descovich said. "We know that parents have to have a right to opt out of things that violate their religious beliefs."

The lawsuit follows a June 15, 2026, school board meeting in which Ann Ciccarelli, president of the Chatham School District Board of Education, said the district was not legally bound by the Mirabelli decision and instead was required to follow the New Jersey Department of Education's 2018 guidance on transgender students.

DAD OF THIRD-GRADE GIRL IN MASSACHUSETTS ALLEGEDLY BARGED IN ON BY TRANS STUDENT IN BATHROOM CALLS FOR ACTION

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

But New Jersey Attorney General Matthew Platkin acknowledged that Policy 5756 is not mandatory, according to NJ Spotlight News.

"The guidance violates both Maribel and it violates Mahmood and, so you know there's a lot of crossover and confusion here, but what it comes down to is the school board. The school has a duty and responsibility to protect constitutional rights of the citizens in its community of its employees of its students of its families, and it is not doing that," Descovich said.

Ferrara told Fox News Digital that since parents began speaking out against the policy, they have been subjected to threats and intimidation. He said that one family has had police security outside their homes.

"This is what happens when you oppose these policies," Ferrara told Fox News Digital. "You basically are going to be subjected to a vicious public backlash by ideologues who are totally intolerant of basically the normal point of view on this issue."

item.title: I'm Gen Z: If the GOP wants my vote, stop the speeches and fix the housing crisis
item.description: Republicans must use the Dallas midterm political convention next week to address housing, cost of living, and free speech to win over Gen-Z voters.
item.content:encoded:
I’m going to Dallas next week to attend the 2026 Republican Midterm Convention. I'm not going for the merch and not for the parties. I’m going because Republicans are about to get two nights of primetime television, the first midterm political convention in American history, and if we waste that stage just talking to ourselves, we will deserve a Blue Wave on Election Day, November 3.

Let me say the quiet part at full volume: We are running against a Democratic Party that has stopped pretending. Democratic socialists are winning primaries, and their platform is not "more Medicaid." It is a new constitution, public ownership of the economy and the end of the United States Senate. 

President Trump has called members of the DSA communists, and he wasn’t being cute. If we lose Congress to that coalition, it will not be because America secretly wanted commissars. It will be because we could not look a 20-year-old like me in the eye and tell him why our side will let him buy a house, keep a paycheck, and speak without getting hurt.

REPUBLICAN PARTY TO HOST HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION IN DALLAS, TRUMP ANNOUNCES ON TRUTH SOCIAL

Gen Z is not a lost cause. Young men already moved toward the GOP in 2024. Housing is their number-one issue, and the cost of living is the country’s number-one issue. They do not care about our process stories. They care whether this country still works for people who were not born holding a down payment.

So here is what I want to hear from that stage at American Airlines Center: Highlight the wins that are real, and stop burying them under slogans.

The border is not a vibe. Illegal crossings collapsed, catch-and-release is dead, and net migration went negative for the first time in half a century. Fentanyl deaths dropped more than 20 percent in a year. That is not "tough talk." That is fewer dead classmates.

REPUBLICANS CAN WIN THE MIDTERMS IF THEY JUST STOP UNDERSELLING SUCCESS

The Working Families Tax Cuts made the 2017 rates permanent, with no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security, Trump Accounts for kids, and a bigger Child Tax Credit. That is money that stays with a bartender, a welder or a nurse working a double. Do not assume young voters already know, because their algorithm has been feeding them the opposite story.

School choice is expanding, hostages are coming home, and factories are being announced again. And when we remember Charlie Kirk, who was killed on a campus last September for doing the one thing Gen Z actually respects — showing up and arguing in public — it should not be a 90-second tribute and a cut to commercial. His death is the argument. If a 31-year-old can be shot for debating college kids, free speech is not a branding exercise. It is a survival issue.

WHO WANTS THEIR CHILD TO BE A MILLIONAIRE? TRUMP HAS GIVEN YOU THAT CHANCE

Then make promises that sound like they were written by someone who has paid rent in this decade.

Promise a housing offensive that treats supply like a national emergency: Smash the zoning cartel, speed permits, and stop turning every starter home into a museum piece for people who already own one. Promise a first-time-buyer track that is not another 400-page bill named after a senator. Promise the next Congress will ban members from trading individual stocks. Young people think the game is rigged, and they are not crazy.

THE AMERICAN DREAM NOW COMES WITH A ZIP CODE: HERE'S WHERE STARTER HOMES ARE STILL WITHIN REACH

Promise trade schools and apprenticeships with the same intensity we give tax rates. A generation drowning in degrees and debt does not need another lecture that college is the dream. 

They need a path that does not require a $90,000 ticket to learn a job America actually needs. Promise energy abundance like you mean it, not as a culture-war prop but as a cost-of-living policy. Electricity, gas, groceries, and rent move together. If we cannot explain that chain on national television, we will lose affordability to people who will nationalize the grocery store and call it compassion.

Promise campuses will not be permission slips for political violence, that boys are not a problem to be managed, and that we will stop importing labor to undercut the kid who stayed and showed up for work.

That is the speech, not "our values" and not "the swamp": specific, measurable, and aimed at the cohort that can still flip.

Democrats want this convention to look like a circus, and that is fine, because circuses draw a crowd. The question is what the crowd hears when the lights hit. Vice President JD Vance opens Wednesday, and President Trump closes Thursday. Between those two nights, the country will decide whether Republicans are a governing party with a future or a nostalgia act with better production value.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

I am tired of hearing that Gen Z is "too far gone." That is what losers say, so they don’t have to do the work. This generation is transactional, anti-incumbent, and allergic to being lied to. They voted against Trump, then they voted for him, and they will vote against us just as fast if we talk like consultants. Next week is the cleanest shot we will get before November: primetime in Dallas.

If we cannot win that argument, we don’t get to blame the media, the map, or the kids. We get to blame the people who had the microphone and used it to congratulate themselves.

See you in Dallas. Don’t blow it.
